newsitem.title: GERMANY: Central bankers happy with EMI convergence report.
newsitem.headline: Central bankers happy with EMI convergence report.

text.p: Central bank governors leaving a meeting of the European Monetary Institute council on Tuesday made positive comments about an EMI report on monetary union convergence due to be published on Wednesday.
"It was very satisfactory, technically speaking, a very satisfying report," Bank of England governor Eddie George said when asked for comment by journalists.
French central bank governor Jean-Claude Trichet said the meeting, at which the report was a central topic, had gone well. "Everything went very well," Trichet said.
The meeting went on until 1700 GMT, around two hours longer than normal.
The report is due to be published at 1130 GMT on Wednesday.
It is due to examine the progress European Union countries have made toward currency union.
The EMI, whose decision-making council comprises European Union central bank governors and its current president, Alexandre Lamfalussy, is the forerunner for the future European Central Bank.
